audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does the precompile correctly trigger out-of-gas revert when available_gas < 6900?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: RunPrecompiledContract computes gasCost = p.RequiredGas(input). For p256Verify, RequiredGas always returns 6900 (params.P256VerifyGas). The conditional `suppliedGas < gasCost` correctly triggers ErrOutOfGas when gas < 6900. When suppliedGas >= 6900, execution proceeds to Run(). The abstract domain of gas is correctly partitioned: [0, 6899] → OOG, [6900, 2^64-1] → execute.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Call path: Transaction → EVM.Call (evm.go:286) → RunPrecompiledContract(p256Verify, input, gas, logger). P256Verify is at address 0x0100 in PrecompiledContractsOsaka. An attacker can control gas via CALL opcode. At suppliedGas=6899: returns (nil, 0, ErrOutOfGas). At suppliedGas=6900: gasCost=6900, suppliedGas-=6900→0, Run() executes, returns (output, 0, nil). All gas consumed in both cases at boundary.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via any transaction that CALLs address 0x0100 with controlled gas parameter.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: p256Verify reverts ↔ suppliedGas < 6900. PROOF: RequiredGas returns constant 6900. Run() never returns error (returns nil,nil for invalid input; true32Byte,nil for valid). The ONLY error path is the gas check. QED. The invariant holds. On OOG, remainingGas=0 is returned, consistent with standard EVM out-of-gas semantics.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: externally reachable via Transaction, attacker-controlled gas parameter.

audit_items.title: Verify EVM-to-Precompile Gas Consumption: Is remaining gas fully consumed on out-of-gas revert?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: When suppliedGas < gasCost: returns (nil, 0, ErrOutOfGas). The remainingGas=0 means all supplied gas is consumed. The EVM caller handles ErrOutOfGas by not refunding gas.

phase2.symbolic_execution: suppliedGas=100, gasCost=6900 → 100<6900 → return (nil, 0, ErrOutOfGas). remainingGas=0. In evm.go Call(), the error causes gas to not be returned to caller. Consistent with standard EVM out-of-gas behavior.
phase2.reachability: Reachable via any CALL to p256Verify with insufficient gas.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: On OOG, remainingGas = 0 (all gas consumed). PROOF: The return statement `return nil, 0, ErrOutOfGas` explicitly sets remainingGas to 0. The EVM does not refund any gas on OOG errors. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: externally reachable via Transaction.

audit_items.title: Verify Precompile Revert Exclusivity: Does the precompile revert ONLY for gas < 6900?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: RunPrecompiledContract has exactly one error path: suppliedGas < gasCost → ErrOutOfGas. p256Verify.Run() never returns an error: invalid input length → (nil, nil); invalid signature → (nil, nil); valid signature → (true32Byte, nil). Therefore the ONLY revert condition is gas < 6900.

phase2.symbolic_execution: With gas>=6900: RequiredGas=6900, gas check passes. Run(malformed_input) → (nil, nil) no error. Run(invalid_sig) → (nil, nil) no error. Run(valid_sig) → (true32Byte, nil) no error. No revert possible with sufficient gas.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable. Attacker can send any input with any gas amount.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: p256Verify reverts ↔ suppliedGas < 6900. PROOF: Forward direction proven in CHK-0001#15. Reverse: when gas>=6900, gas check passes, Run() never errors (all code paths return nil error). QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: externally reachable, attacker-controlled.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 hash of RLP-encoded trie deterministic regardless of insertion order?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The Merkle Patricia Trie is a canonical trie: given the same set of (key, value) pairs, the trie structure is uniquely determined regardless of insertion order. Each node has a canonical RLP encoding. Keccak256 is deterministic. Therefore: same key-value set → same trie → same RLP → same keccak256 hash.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Insert {A:1, B:2} vs {B:2, A:1}: both produce identical trie structure. The trie resolves via node splitting/merging. hashRoot() calls h.hash(root, true) which recursively hashes all nodes. The RLP encoding of each node type (shortNode, fullNode) is deterministic. hashData uses crypto.KeccakState which is deterministic.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable: any transaction modifying state affects the trie.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: For any set S of (key, value) pairs, root(trie(S)) is unique. PROOF: MPT canonical structure theorem + deterministic RLP + deterministic keccak256. This is a fundamental property of the MPT design proven in the Yellow Paper. Geth's implementation follows the spec correctly.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: core consensus property, externally reachable.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the 32-byte RLP encoding threshold consistently enforced in encode_internal_node?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: In hasher.hash(), the condition `len(enc) < 32 && !force` determines embedding vs hashing. For both shortNode and fullNode: encoding < 32 bytes → embed inline (return raw bytes); encoding >= 32 bytes → hash via keccak256. The threshold uses strict less-than (<32), meaning exactly 32 bytes triggers hashing. This matches the Yellow Paper specification.

phase2.symbolic_execution: len(enc)=31, force=false → 31<32 && !false = true → embedded inline. len(enc)=32, force=false → 32<32 = false → hashed. len(enc)=31, force=true → 31<32 && !true = false → hashed (root always hashed). Boundary condition at exactly 32 bytes is correctly handled.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable: any state change triggers trie hashing.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Nodes with RLP encoding >= 32 bytes are hashed; < 32 bytes are embedded (unless force=true for root). PROOF: The conditional `len(enc) < 32 && !force` exactly implements this. The `force` parameter is true only for the root node (hashRoot passes force=true). QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: consensus-critical encoding threshold.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is storage_root validated as non-None for all Account nodes in encode_node?

code_scope.reason: In geth's Go implementation, the trie stores raw byte values (valueNode). Account encoding happens at a higher level (core/state) before insertion into the trie. The trie itself does not distinguish Account vs other values - it stores already-encoded byte slices.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth's trie stores valueNode ([]byte). Account RLP encoding including storage_root is handled by core/state/statedb.go before trie insertion. The state object ensures storage_root is computed before account commitment. There is no None/nil storage_root possible at the trie level because accounts are fully serialized before storage.

phase2.symbolic_execution: StateDB.Commit → stateObject.commit → computes storageRoot → encodes Account with storageRoot → trie.Update(address, encodedAccount). The storage root is always computed before account encoding.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction but the encoding pipeline prevents nil storage_root.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Account nodes always have a valid storage_root. PROOF: The StateDB commit pipeline ensures storage tries are committed before account encoding. The Account RLP encoding requires a Root field (common.Hash, 32 bytes). Go's type system prevents nil Hash values. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope but architectural: geth's type system and commit pipeline prevent this class of bug.

The hasher handles: shortNode (leaf/extension), fullNode (branch), hashNode (reference), valueNode (raw bytes). No fork-specific types need handling because all values are pre-encoded to bytes before trie insertion.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does copy_trie produce true isolation between original and copy?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Trie.Copy() creates a new Trie struct with: copyNode(t.root) for deep-copying the node tree, new opTracer via copy(), new prevalueTracer via Copy(). The key question is whether copyNode provides deep isolation. In geth, copyNode recursively copies all node structures, ensuring mutations to the copy don't affect the original.

phase2.symbolic_execution: original := trie; copy := trie.Copy(); copy.Update(key, value). The copy has a deep-copied node tree, so updates to the copy create new nodes without modifying the original's nodes. The reader (database reference) is shared but read-only.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable: re-org processing may copy tries.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Mutations to copy do not affect original. PROOF: copyNode creates deep copies of all mutable node structures. The shared reader is read-only. New node allocations during updates don't alias with original nodes. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: copy isolation is critical for re-org safety.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does trie_set properly delete keys when value equals default?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Trie.Update(key, value) checks len(value) == 0. If empty, it calls delete(). If non-empty, it calls insert(). This ensures that setting a key to the default (empty) value removes it from the trie, preventing phantom entries.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Update(key, []byte{}) → len([]byte{})=0 → delete(root, nil, k) → removes node from trie. Subsequent Get(key) returns nil. State root reflects the removal.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction (SSTORE with zero value).

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: trie_set(k, default) ⇒ key k is removed from trie. PROOF: len(value)==0 triggers delete() which removes the node and restructures the trie (merging/pruning nodes as needed). No phantom entries remain. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: state consistency property.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is trie_set/trie_get roundtrip guaranteed for non-default values?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: For non-empty values: Update(key, value) stores value as valueNode(value) via insert(). Get(key) traverses the trie and returns the stored valueNode bytes. The roundtrip is guaranteed because: (1) non-empty values bypass the delete path, (2) valueNode stores the exact bytes, (3) Get returns the exact stored bytes.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Update(k, []byte{0x00}) → len=1≠0 → insert(root, nil, k, valueNode{0x00}). Get(k) → traverse trie → find valueNode{0x00} → return []byte{0x00}. Roundtrip verified. No type confusion: all values are stored as raw byte slices.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: ∀ non-empty v: Get(k) after Update(k,v) returns v. PROOF: insert() stores valueNode(v) at the canonical path for k. Get() traverses the same path and retrieves the valueNode. valueNode is a []byte type alias. No implicit conversions or comparisons. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: fundamental data integrity property.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is nibble_list_to_compact encoding is_leaf flag and parity correct?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: hexToCompact encodes hex nibbles to compact format. terminator = hasTerm(hex) ? 1 : 0. buf[0] = terminator << 5 sets bit 5 for leaf (0x20). If odd length: buf[0] |= 1<<4 (0x10) sets parity flag. First nibble embedded in low nibble of buf[0]. Result: high_nibble = 2*is_leaf + parity. Exactly matches Yellow Paper specification.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Leaf, even (hex=[1,2,16]): terminator=1, buf[0]=0x20, len=2(even), buf[0]=0x20 → high nibble=2 ✓. Leaf, odd (hex=[1,2,3,16]): terminator=1, buf[0]=0x20, len=3(odd), buf[0]=0x20|0x10|1=0x31 → high nibble=3 ✓. Extension, even (hex=[1,2]): terminator=0, buf[0]=0x00 → high nibble=0 ✓. Extension, odd (hex=[1,2,3]): buf[0]=0x10|1=0x11 → high nibble=1 ✓.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P (Merkle proof verification).

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: first_byte_high_nibble = 2*is_leaf + (len(nibbles) % 2). PROOF: terminator<<5 contributes 2*is_leaf to high nibble. (len&1==1)<<4 contributes parity to high nibble. These are the only modifications to buf[0] high nibble. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: encoding correctness affects Merkle proof verification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are bytes_to_nibble_list and nibble_list_to_compact mutual inverses?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: keybytesToHex converts bytes→nibbles (each byte to 2 nibbles + terminator 16). hexToCompact converts nibbles→compact (encoding is_leaf and parity in first byte). compactToHex converts compact→nibbles (reverse operation). The roundtrip keybytesToHex→hexToCompact→compactToHex→... preserves the original data.

phase2.symbolic_execution: bytes=[0xAB,0xCD]: keybytesToHex→[0xA,0xB,0xC,0xD,16]. hexToCompact→[0x20,0xAB,0xCD] (leaf, even). compactToHex→[0xA,0xB,0xC,0xD,16]. Roundtrip verified. Extension case: hex=[0xA,0xB]. hexToCompact→[0x00,0xAB]. compactToHex→[0xA,0xB]. Roundtrip verified.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P proof paths.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: compactToHex(hexToCompact(x)) = x for valid hex nibble lists. PROOF: hexToCompact encodes the terminator flag and parity in buf[0]. compactToHex uses keybytesToHex to decode, then strips the terminator flag and applies odd-flag chop. The operations are inverse by construction. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: encoding roundtrip critical for proof verification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_node produce non-empty output for all valid values?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: encodeShortNode and encodeFullNode use RLP encoding via rlp.EncoderBuffer. RLP encoding of any non-nil struct always produces non-empty output (minimum: a length prefix byte). A shortNode always has Key and Val fields. A fullNode always has at least one non-nil child. Therefore RLP encoding always produces non-empty bytes.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Minimal shortNode: Key=[16] (single terminator), Val=valueNode{0x00}. RLP encoding: [0xC2, 0x20, 0x00] (3 bytes, non-empty). Minimal fullNode: one child. RLP encoding: at least 17-element list with one non-nil entry. Always non-empty.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: For all valid trie nodes, RLP encoding produces non-empty output. PROOF: RLP encoding of any value produces at least one byte (the type/length prefix). Trie nodes are always valid structs with required fields. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: empty encoding would crash nodes.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 key hashing enforced for secured tries?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth uses StateTrie (secure trie) for the state trie. StateTrie wraps Trie and hashes all keys with keccak256 before insertion. This is enforced in the StateTrie methods (Get, Update, Delete) which hash the key before delegating to the underlying Trie. The state trie always uses keccak256 key hashing.

phase2.symbolic_execution: StateTrie.Update(address, value) → hashKey(address) → keccak256(address) → trie.Update(hashedKey, value). The hashing is applied transparently. An attacker cannot bypass it because StateTrie is the only interface used for state storage.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: All state trie keys are keccak256-hashed. PROOF: StateDB uses StateTrie exclusively. StateTrie.Update/Get/Delete all hash keys via hashKey() before delegating to Trie. There is no public API to bypass hashing. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: key hashing prevents DoS via trie shape manipulation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is get_storage_root callback correctly invoked with proper Address?

code_scope.reason: In geth, storage root computation is handled by StateDB/stateObject, not via a callback mechanism. Each stateObject maintains its own storage trie. During commit, the storage trie root is computed and set as the account's StorageRoot field.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth does not use a callback-based storage root computation. Instead, each stateObject (representing an account) owns a storage trie. During StateDB.Commit(), each dirty stateObject commits its storage trie (computing the root hash) and then encodes the account with the computed storage root. This architectural choice eliminates the callback integrity concern.

phase2.symbolic_execution: StateDB.Commit() → for each dirty object → object.commit() → storageTrie.Commit() → returns storageRoot → account.Root = storageRoot → encode account → state trie.Update(addr, encodedAccount). The storage root is always fresh and correct.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Each account's storage_root correctly reflects its storage trie state. PROOF: The commit pipeline ensures storage tries are committed before account encoding. The storage root is the direct result of storageTrie.Commit(). No callback mechanism means no callback integrity issues. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: critical state consistency property.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does empty trie produce correct EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: hashRoot() checks if root==nil. If nil, returns types.EmptyRootHash.Bytes(). EmptyRootHash = keccak256(RLP('')) = keccak256(0x80) = 0x56e81f171bcc55a6ff8345e692c0f86e5b48e01b996cadc001622fb5e363b421. This is the standard empty trie root used across all Ethereum implementations.

phase2.symbolic_execution: New empty trie: root=nil → hashRoot() → types.EmptyRootHash.Bytes() → 32-byte constant. Trie with all entries deleted: root becomes nil after delete operations → hashRoot() → EmptyRootHash. Commit() also returns EmptyRootHash when root is nil.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction, EngineAPI.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: empty_trie.root() == EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT. PROOF: When root is nil, hashRoot() returns the constant EmptyRootHash which equals keccak256(RLP('')). This constant is defined in core/types/hashes.go and matches the Ethereum specification. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: consensus-critical empty state handling.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is root() output always exactly 32 bytes?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Empty trie: EmptyRootHash.Bytes() → common.Hash → 32 bytes. Non-empty trie: h.hash(root, true) with force=true. The force=true parameter bypasses inline embedding (`!force` is false), so the root always goes through hashData(). hashData() allocates make([]byte, 32) and reads keccak256 into it → exactly 32 bytes.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Small root (enc < 32 bytes), force=true: `len(enc) < 32 && !true` = false → hashData(enc) → 32 bytes. Large root (enc >= 32 bytes), force=true: hash path → hashData(enc) → 32 bytes. All paths produce 32 bytes.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P, Transaction, EngineAPI.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: |root()| = 32 bytes always. PROOF: Case 1: root==nil → EmptyRootHash (32 bytes). Case 2: root!=nil, force=true → hashData always returns 32 bytes (keccak256 output size). No other cases exist. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: non-32-byte root would cause validation failures.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does patricialize correctly handle common prefix extension nodes?

code_scope.reason: Geth does not use a separate patricialize function. The trie structure is built incrementally via insert/delete operations that correctly create and maintain shortNode (extension/leaf) and fullNode (branch) nodes. Extension nodes are created when keys share a common prefix.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth builds the trie incrementally. When inserting a key that shares a prefix with an existing shortNode, the insert function splits the shortNode at the divergence point, creating an extension node for the common prefix and a branch node for the diverging paths. This is equivalent to the patricialize algorithm.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Insert key [1,2,3,4]: creates shortNode([1,2,3,4], value). Insert key [1,2,5,6]: common prefix=[1,2]. Split: shortNode([1,2], fullNode{3:shortNode([4],v1), 5:shortNode([6],v2)}). Extension node correctly created for common prefix.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Common prefix extension nodes are correctly created during trie operations. PROOF: The insert function in trie.go handles prefix splitting by: (1) computing common prefix via prefixLen, (2) splitting at the divergence point, (3) creating extension shortNode for the common prefix. This is correct by the MPT specification.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: incorrect extension nodes produce wrong state roots.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are Account/Receipt/Uint rejected at internal branch value positions?

code_scope.reason: In geth, the trie stores raw bytes (valueNode). There is no type system at the trie level that distinguishes Account/Receipt/Uint. All values are pre-serialized to bytes before trie insertion. Branch (fullNode) value positions (Children[16]) store valueNode bytes. The type safety concern does not apply to geth's architecture.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth's trie is type-agnostic. It stores []byte values. The fullNode.Children[16] position holds a valueNode ([]byte). There is no risk of Account/Receipt objects being placed at branch positions because the trie only accepts byte slices.

phase2.symbolic_execution: trie.Update(key, rlpEncodedAccount) → insert stores valueNode(rlpEncodedAccount) at leaf position. Branch values (Children[16]) are only set when a key exactly matches the branch level. The value is always a byte slice.
phase2.reachability: Architecture prevents this issue.

phase3.invariant: By design, geth's trie stores raw bytes at all value positions. Type-specific encoding/decoding happens at higher layers. No assertion needed at the trie level.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope but architectural: Go's type system and geth's architecture prevent this issue.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does patricialize guarantee termination through increasing level?

code_scope.reason: Geth uses iterative insert/delete operations rather than a recursive patricialize. However, the StackTrie (trie/stacktrie.go) builds the trie in-order and guarantees termination. The standard Trie operations are bounded by key length (max 64 nibbles for 32-byte keys).

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Trie operations in geth traverse the key nibble-by-nibble. Each recursive call in insert/delete consumes at least one nibble from the key. Since keys have finite length (max 64 nibbles for 32-byte keccak256 hashes), recursion depth is bounded by key length. This guarantees termination.

phase2.symbolic_execution: insert(root, prefix, key, value): at each recursion, the key prefix grows by at least one nibble. Maximum depth = len(key) = 64 (for hashed keys). No infinite recursion possible.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Trie operations terminate. PROOF: Each recursive call in insert/delete/get consumes at least one nibble from the remaining key. Keys are finite (max 64 nibbles for state trie). Therefore recursion depth ≤ 64. No stack overflow possible for reasonable stack sizes. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: termination guarantee prevents DoS.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 collision resistance assumed correctly?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth uses the standard Keccak-256 hash function (SHA-3 candidate). Keccak-256 has 128-bit collision resistance (birthday bound on 256-bit output). No known practical collision attacks exist. The implementation uses golang.org/x/crypto/sha3 which is a well-audited library.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Keccak-256 is used consistently across the codebase: trie hashing, address derivation, state root computation, transaction hashing. The collision resistance assumption (2^-128 probability) is fundamental to Ethereum's security model.
phase2.reachability: Foundational cryptographic assumption.

phase3.invariant: ASSUMPTION: Keccak-256 is collision-resistant. This is a standard cryptographic assumption validated by extensive cryptanalysis. No known attacks reduce the collision resistance below 2^128 operations. The assumption is correctly relied upon by geth.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: foundational assumption. No implementation vulnerability.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding canonical and deterministic?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth's RLP encoder (rlp package) produces canonical encoding: no leading zeros in length prefixes, shortest possible encoding for each value, deterministic field ordering (struct fields in declaration order). The encoder is deterministic: same input always produces same output.

phase2.symbolic_execution: RLP encoding of a trie node struct produces the same bytes regardless of call context. The encoding follows the Ethereum Yellow Paper RLP specification. Go structs have deterministic field ordering. No ambiguity in encoding.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P, Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: RLP encoding is canonical and deterministic. PROOF: Geth's rlp package produces shortest-form encoding (canonical RLP as specified in the Yellow Paper). Struct field ordering is deterministic in Go. Same struct values → same RLP bytes → same hash. This is validated by extensive cross-client test vectors. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: RLP canonicality is critical for consensus.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are nibble values validated in range [0, 15]?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: keybytesToHex converts each byte b to two nibbles: b/16 and b%16. For any byte value [0,255]: b/16 ∈ [0,15] and b%16 ∈ [0,15]. The terminator value 16 is used only as a sentinel (not a nibble). Therefore all generated nibbles are in [0,15].

phase2.symbolic_execution: For b=0xFF: 0xFF/16=15, 0xFF%16=15 → nibbles [15,15] ✓. For b=0x00: 0/16=0, 0%16=0 → nibbles [0,0] ✓. Terminator 16 is appended separately and handled by hasTerm(). hexToCompact strips the terminator before packing nibbles.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P (Merkle proof paths).

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: All nibbles from keybytesToHex are in [0,15]. PROOF: For any byte b: b/16 ≤ 255/16 = 15 and b%16 ≤ 15. The terminator (16) is not a nibble but a sentinel marker. Nibbles received from P2P are re-derived from compact encoding via compactToHex which uses keybytesToHex internally. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: nibble range validation prevents proof forgery.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is P2P block state root verification enforced?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth validates block state roots in the block validation pipeline. After executing all transactions in a block, the resulting state root is compared against the block header's state root. If they don't match, the block is rejected. This is enforced in core/block_validator.go's ValidateState function.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Block received from P2P → blockchain.InsertChain → process transactions → compute state root → ValidateState compares computed root vs header.Root. Mismatch → block rejected with consensus error.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P block propagation.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: All accepted blocks have verified state roots. PROOF: InsertChain calls process() which executes transactions and computes state root, then calls validator.ValidateState() which compares roots. No code path accepts a block without state root verification. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: primary defense against forged blocks.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is patricialize complexity bounded by O(N * K)?

code_scope.reason: Geth's trie operations have O(K) complexity per operation where K is the key length (64 nibbles for state trie). For N operations, total complexity is O(N*K). The gas system bounds N per block.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Each trie insert/delete/get operation traverses the key path from root to leaf, consuming one nibble per step. Key length K=64 nibbles (for keccak256-hashed keys). Therefore each operation is O(K)=O(64). For N state changes in a block, total complexity is O(N*64). The block gas limit bounds N.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Worst case: N accounts with long common prefixes. Each insert still traverses at most K=64 nibbles. The trie structure may have longer paths due to extension nodes, but each path is bounded by K. Total: O(N*K).
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via Transaction.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: Trie operation complexity is O(N*K) where N=number of entries, K=key length. PROOF: Each operation traverses at most K=64 nibbles. Hashing during commit is also O(N*K) since each node is visited once. The gas system ensures N is bounded per block. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: complexity bounds prevent gas/computation asymmetry DoS.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are state sync trie nodes verified against known root?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Geth's trie sync (trie/sync.go) downloads trie nodes from peers and verifies them against known root hashes. The Sync struct maintains a queue of requested nodes. When a node is received, its keccak256 hash is computed and compared against the expected hash (from the parent node reference). This chain of verification anchors at the known state root.

phase2.symbolic_execution: Start with known root hash R. Request node for R from peer. Receive node N. Verify keccak256(RLP(N)) == R. If valid, extract child references from N. For each child reference H (32 bytes), request child node. Verify keccak256(RLP(child)) == H. Chain continues to leaves.
phase2.reachability: Externally reachable via P2P state sync.

phase3.invariant: INVARIANT: All synced trie nodes are verified against a chain of trust anchored at the known root. PROOF: The sync process only accepts nodes whose keccak256 hash matches the expected reference. The 32-byte threshold for inline vs hash references is correctly handled. Invalid nodes are rejected and re-requested. QED.
phase3.scope_filter: In-scope: invalid sync nodes could corrupt local state.
